title: 1950 Australian National Airways Douglas DC-4 crash
summary: The Amana departed Perth for Adelaide but crashed 22 minutes after takeoff while flying at unusually low altitude. Witnesses observed rough engine running and backfiring; engines periodically lost power completely. Investigation found significant corrosion product and water in the fuel system of at least two engines, which caused rough running and temporary loss of power from all engines.
probable_cause: Water in the fuel system caused corrosion and loss of power from all engines on at least one occasion during the climb.

factors.evidence: a significant amount of corrosion product was found in the fuel system within two of the engines
temporary loss of power from all engines on at least one occasion
aircraft was flying at a lower altitude than usual for the daily Skymaster services
crashed 22 minutes after take-off, 35 mi east of Perth Airport
All 29 occupants were killed in the accident either from multiple injuries and burns, or from incineration

events.text: Amana departed Perth Airport at 9:55 pm for Adelaide
Radio report received from Amana at 10:00 pm advising it was on course and climbing to 9,000 feet
Aircraft heard flying low over York area with changing engine noise; all engine noise ceased briefly then returned as very loud high-pitched scream
Bright flash of white light observed 28 nmi east of Perth Airport, followed by loud crashing noise and yellow glow of fire
Trans Australia Airlines aircraft passed over band of fire on ground; Amana had failed to report position at Cunderdin
